mensagens.content: @contrato.txt

This project already contains a CPU that was generated and APPROVED by the official judge for the PREVIOUS specification (RV32I, monociclo). The specification has changed. Your job is to understand the project and plan the SMALLEST change that satisfies the new specification; nothing is modified yet.

Before planning, every existing test was run again on the approved CPU (baseline):
```json
{
 "isa": "rv32i",
 "componentes": {
  "immediate_generator": {
   "passaram": 5,
   "total": 5
  },
  "register_file": {
   "passaram": 5,
   "total": 5
  },
  "alu": {
   "passaram": 5,
   "total": 5
  },
  "decoder": {
   "passaram": 5,
   "total": 5
  },
  "cpu": {
   "passaram": 5,
   "total": 5
  }
 },
 "spec_riscv_test": "40/40 casos"
}
```

Instructions required now that were not required before: mul, mulh, mulhsu, mulhu, div, divu, rem, remu

Diff of the system contract (previous -> new):
```diff
--- contrato anterior
+++ contrato novo
@@ -8,3 +8,3 @@
 
-- RV32I single cycle
+- RV32IM single cycle
 
@@ -83,3 +83,3 @@
 ISA base: RV32I (lui auipc jal jalr beq bne blt bge bltu bgeu lb lh lw lbu lhu sb sh sw addi slti sltiu xori ori andi slli srli srai add sub sll slt sltu xor srl sra or and).
-RV32M is NOT required, and the entity `cpu` has no generics: do not add one.
+RV32M (mul mulh mulhsu mulhu div divu rem remu) is required: decode opcode 0110011 with funct7 = 0000001. Implement these operations in generated VHDL, including RISC-V division-by-zero and signed-overflow semantics. The entity `cpu` has no generics: the ISA is fixed by specs/cpu.md, so the CPU always implements the M instructions.
 Microarchitecture declared in specs/cpu.md: monociclo.
@@ -290,2 +290,79 @@
 
+# RV32M Implementation Reference
+# RV32M — referência de implementação
+
+Fonte: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA, extensão "M" para multiplicação e divisão
+inteiras, versão 2.0 (RISC-V International, CC-BY-4.0).
+
+Este arquivo só vale quando `specs/cpu.md` declara **RV32IM**. Ele completa
+`riscv-rv32i.md`, que continua valendo inteiro: RV32IM = RV32I + M. Com
+**RV32I** este arquivo não vai para a IA e a CPU não implementa nenhuma
+instrução abaixo.
+
+## Codificação
+
+Todas as instruções M são R-type, com `opcode = 0110011` (`0x33`, o mesmo do
+OP do RV32I) e `funct7 = 0000001` (`0x01`). O `funct7` é o que separa M de
+ADD/SUB/shifts/lógica: no RV32I ele vale `0x00` ou `0x20`.
+
+| Instrução | `funct3` | `funct7` | Resultado em `rd` |
+|---|---:|---:|---|
+| MUL | `0x0` | `0x01` | 32 bits baixos de `rs1 × rs2` |
+| MULH | `0x1` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `signed(rs1) × signed(rs2)` |
+| MULHSU | `0x2` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `signed(rs1) × unsigned(rs2)` |
+| MULHU | `0x3` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `unsigned(rs1) × unsigned(rs2)` |
+| DIV | `0x4` | `0x01` | quociente signed, arredondado para zero |
+| DIVU | `0x5` | `0x01` | quociente unsigned |
+| REM | `0x6` | `0x01` | resto signed; o sinal é o do dividendo (`rs1`) |
+| REMU | `0x7` | `0x01` | resto unsigned |
+
+## Regras gerais
+
+- O produto completo tem 64 bits. MUL devolve os bits `[31:0]` e é o mesmo
+  para operandos signed ou unsigned. MULH, MULHSU e MULHU devolvem os bits
+  `[63:32]`.
+- MULHSU trata `rs1` como signed e `rs2` como unsigned. Não troque a ordem.
+- Divisão e resto truncam para zero: `-7 / 2 = -3` e `-7 rem 2 = -1`.
+- Nenhuma instrução M gera exceção, trap ou estado extra. `rd = x0` continua
+  sendo ignorado.
+- No contrato monociclo de `specs/cpu.md`, uma instrução completa por borda de
+  subida: o resultado de MUL e DIV precisa estar pronto no mesmo ciclo.
+
+## Casos especiais obrigatórios
+
+A divisão por zero e o overflow têm resultado definido pela ISA. A CPU deve
+produzir exatamente estes valores (`x` é o dividendo `rs1`):
+
+| Caso | DIV | DIVU | REM | REMU |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| divisor = 0 | `-1` (`0xFFFFFFFF`) | `2^32 - 1` (`0xFFFFFFFF`) | `x` | `x` |
+| overflow: `x = -2^31` (`0x80000000`) e divisor = `-1` | `-2^31` (`0x80000000`) | (não se aplica) | `0` | (não se aplica) |
+
+## Exemplos para conferir
+
+| Instrução | `rs1` | `rs2` | `rd` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| MUL | `0x00000007` | `0xFFFFFFFD` (-3) | `0xFFFFFFEB` (-21) |
+| MULH | `0x80000000` | `0x80000000` | `0x40000000` |
+| MULHSU | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) | `0xFFFFFFFF` | `0xFFFFFFFF` |
+| MULHU | `0xFFFFFFFF` | `0xFFFFFFFF` | `0xFFFFFFFE` |
+| DIV | `0xFFFFFFF9` (-7) | `0x00000002` | `0xFFFFFFFD` (-3) |
+| DIVU | `0xFFFFFFF9` | `0x00000002` | `0x7FFFFFFC` |
+| REM | `0xFFFFFFF9` (-7) | `0x00000002` | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) |
+| REMU | `0xFFFFFFF9` | `0x00000002` | `0x00000001` |
+| DIV | `0x00000005` | `0x00000000` | `0xFFFFFFFF` |
+| REM | `0x00000005` | `0x00000000` | `0x00000005` |
+| DIV | `0x80000000` | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) | `0x80000000` |
+| REM | `0x80000000` | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) | `0x00000000` |
+
+## Notas para VHDL (`numeric_std`)
+
+- `signed(a) * signed(b)` com operandos de 32 bits dá 64 bits. Para MULHSU,
+  estenda `rs1` com sinal e `rs2` com zero até 33 bits, multiplique como
+  `signed` (66 bits) e pegue os bits `[63:32]`.
+- `/` e `rem` de `numeric_std` truncam para zero e dão ao resto o sinal do
+  dividendo, como a ISA. Mas dividir por zero em VHDL para a simulação com
+  erro: trate divisor zero e o overflow **antes** de calcular, com as saídas
+  da tabela de casos especiais.
+
 # Essential VHDL Generation Specification
```

Current architecture:
- immediate_generator (src/immediate_generator.vhd): Generate sign-extended I-, S-, B-, and J-type immediates, and the zero-extended U-type immediate from the instruction word.
  ports: instr : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); imm_i : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); imm_s : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); imm_b : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); imm_u : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); imm_j : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0)
  depends on: none
- register_file (src/register_file.vhd): Provide 32 32-bit integer registers with two asynchronous read ports, one rising-edge write port, asynchronous active-high reset, and hardwired-zero x0.
  ports: clk : in std_logic; rst : in std_logic; rs1_addr : in std_logic_vector(4 downto 0); rs2_addr : in std_logic_vector(4 downto 0); rs1_data : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); rs2_data : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); rd_addr : in std_logic_vector(4 downto 0); rd_data : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); rd_write : in std_logic
  depends on: none
- alu (src/alu.vhd): Perform RV32I arithmetic, logic, shifts, and signed and unsigned comparisons selected by an operation control input.
  ports: operand_a : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); operand_b : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); alu_control : in std_logic_vector(3 downto 0); result : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); equal : out std_logic; signed_less : out std_logic; unsigned_less : out std_logic
  depends on: none
- decoder (src/decoder.vhd): Decode RV32I instruction opcode and function fields into register-write, memory-write, operand-source, ALU-operation, branch, jump, and writeback-selection controls.
  ports: instr : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); reg_write : out std_logic; mem_write : out std_logic; alu_src_a_pc : out std_logic; alu_src_b_imm : out std_logic; alu_control : out std_logic_vector(3 downto 0); branch_enable : out std_logic; jump : out std_logic; jalr : out std_logic; wb_select : out std_logic_vector(1 downto 0)
  depends on: none
- cpu (src/cpu.vhd): Implement the RV32I single-cycle top level: maintain the PC, instantiate the register file, decoder, ALU, and immediate generator, select branch and jump targets, perform load extraction and extension, and drive the instruction and data buses exactly as specified.
  ports: clk : in std_logic; rst : in std_logic; instr_addr : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); instr_data : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); data_addr : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); data_write : out std_logic; data_width : out std_logic_vector(1 downto 0); data_write_data : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0); data_read_data : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0)
  depends on: immediate_generator, register_file, alu, decoder

Current semantic contract of each block:
## immediate_generator
# Component semantic contract: immediate_generator

## Public interface
```vhdl
entity immediate_generator is
    port(
        instr : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        imm_i : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        imm_s : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        imm_b : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        imm_u : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        imm_j : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0)
    );
end immediate_generator;
```

## Responsibility
Generate sign-extended I-, S-, B-, and J-type immediates, and the zero-extended U-type immediate from the instruction word.

## Timing

`immediate_generator` is purely combinational. Each output must reflect the current `instr` value after combinational propagation settles. No clock or handshake is involved, and changes to `instr` must not require a clock edge.

## Reset

None. The component has no reset input and no reset behavior.

## Behavior

For every 32-bit `instr` value, produce all five immediates concurrently, independent of the opcode or any other instruction field not specified in these formulas. `sext(x)` denotes sign extension of `x` to 32 bits; `||` denotes concatenation.

- `imm_i = sext(instr[31:20])`
- `imm_s = sext(instr[31:25] || instr[11:7])`
- `imm_b = sext(instr[31] || instr[7] || instr[30:25] || instr[11:8] || 0)`
- `imm_u = instr[31:12] || 0x000`
- `imm_j = sext(instr[31] || instr[19:12] || instr[20] || instr[30:21] || 0)`

For B-type, `imm_b[0]=0`, `imm_b[4:1]=instr[11:8]`, `imm_b[10:5]=instr[30:25]`, `imm_b[11]=instr[7]`, and `imm_b[12]=instr[31]`; `imm_b[31:13]` are the sign extension of `instr[31]`.

For J-type, `imm_j[0]=0`, `imm_j[10:1]=instr[30:21]`, `imm_j[11]=instr[20]`, `imm_j[19:12]=instr[19:12]`, and `imm_j[20]=instr[31]`; `imm_j[31:21]` are the sign extension of `instr[31]`.

## Operations

None. There is no encoded selector. All five outputs are generated for every input word.

## Edge cases

- When `instr[31]=0`, the I-, S-, B-, and J-type outputs have zero-filled sign-extension bits.
- When `instr[31]=1`, the I-, S-, B-, and J-type outputs have one-filled sign-extension bits in their respective upper ranges.
- The low bit of `imm_b` and `imm_j` is always zero, regardless of `instr`.
- The low 12 bits of `imm_u` are always zero. Its upper 20 bits are exactly `instr[31:12]`; this is not sign extension.
- Opcode values, including unsupported or otherwise invalid instruction encodings, do not suppress or alter any output.

## Test strategy

Use a combinational Cocotb test: drive `instr`, allow combinational propagation to settle, and compare all five outputs against the formulas in **Behavior**. Do not use clock edges or reset.

1. **Bit mapping, packing, and slicing:** For each `k` from 0 through 31, compare the outputs for `instr=0` with those for `instr = 1 << k`; then, separately, compare the outputs for `instr=0xFFFFFFFF` with those for `instr = 0xFFFFFFFF ^ (1 << k)`. Each comparison pair differs only in bit `k`. Check every output against the formulas after each drive. These tests exercise every source bit, detect omitted or incorrectly included bits, and check constant-zero positions.
2. **Sign extension:** With all bits other than bit 31 held at zero, test `instr=0` and `instr=0x80000000`. Then, separately for each `k` from 0 through 30, compare `instr = 1 << k` with `instr = (1 << k) | 0x80000000`; each pair differs only in bit 31. Check the effects prescribed by the formulas, including the mapped bit and sign-filled upper bits of `imm_i`, `imm_s`, `imm_b`, and `imm_j`. Check that `imm_u[31:12]` includes bit 31 directly and that `imm_u[11:0]` remains zero.
3. **Distinguishable source fields:** Drive fixed nonuniform words, including `0xD5A69B3C` and `0x2B59E6A7`, and check every output. Also construct cases with distinct, nonzero patterns in the input slices used by each immediate formula; check that each output follows its specified slice and ordering, rather than another slice or a reversed ordering. For each comparison, change only the slice or bit under examination while holding all other input bits fixed.
4. **Opcode independence:** For each fixed nonuniform word, vary only `instr[6:0]` across all 128 opcode values. Require all five outputs to match the formulas for the complete current `instr` word. This confirms that no opcode class selects or suppresses an immediate.
5. **Boundary patterns:** Check `instr=0`, `instr=0xFFFFFFFF`, `instr=0x7FFFF000`, and `instr=0x80000000`. These cases must confirm zero and all-one sign extension, the B/J implicit low zero bits, and the U-type zero low 12 bits.


## register_file
# Component semantic contract: register_file

## Public interface
```vhdl
entity register_file is
    port(
        clk : in std_logic;
        rst : in std_logic;
        rs1_addr : in std_logic_vector(4 downto 0);
        rs2_addr : in std_logic_vector(4 downto 0);
        rs1_data : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        rs2_data : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        rd_addr : in std_logic_vector(4 downto 0);
        rd_data : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        rd_write : in std_logic
    );
end register_file;
```

## Responsibility
Provide 32 32-bit integer registers with two asynchronous read ports, one rising-edge write port, asynchronous active-high reset, and hardwired-zero x0.

## Timing

- `rs1_data` and `rs2_data` are asynchronous outputs. Each reflects the value selected by its corresponding address without waiting for a clock edge.
- A write takes effect on a rising edge of `clk` when `rst = '0'` and `rd_write = '1'`. The write uses `rd_addr` and `rd_data` sampled at that edge.
- After a qualifying write edge, asynchronous reads reflect the updated value. A write does not change a register before that edge.
- Asserting reset takes effect asynchronously and does not require a clock edge.

## Reset

- `rst` is active high and asynchronous.
- While `rst = '1'`, every register reads as zero and writes do not take effect, whether or not a clock edge occurs.
- Deasserting reset does not itself modify register values. After reset has been asserted, all registers remain zero until written.
- If reset is asserted at a rising clock edge, reset takes priority over a write.

## Behavior

- The component provides 32 architectural registers, each 32 bits wide. A 5-bit binary address selects the register with that unsigned index.
- `rs1_addr` selects the value presented on `rs1_data`; `rs2_addr` independently selects the value presented on `rs2_data`.
- Address zero always reads as `0x00000000`. Writes to address zero have no effect, regardless of `rd_write` or `rd_data`.
- For addresses 1 through 31, a qualifying write stores the full 32-bit `rd_data` value in the register selected by `rd_addr`.
- `rd_write = '0'` prevents a write. With reset inactive, only a qualifying rising edge can write a register.
- All 5-bit binary addresses from `00000` through `11111` are valid. Behavior for non-binary `std_logic` values on inputs is unspecified.

## Operations

None.

## Edge cases

- Reads of address zero return zero at all times, including during reset and after attempted writes to address zero.
- Reset asserted between clock edges clears all registers without waiting for a clock.
- A write with `rd_write = '0'` does not change a register, even when `rd_addr` and `rd_data` change across rising edges.
- A write to a nonzero address changes only that register; all other registers retain their values.
- There are no invalid binary register addresses or partial-width reads or writes.

## Test strategy

Use representative cases rather than exhaustively enumerating register addresses or write destinations. Use `x0` to check hardwired-zero behavior, a representative nonzero register such as `x5`, and the boundary register `x31`. Exercise both read ports with these selections.

1. **Reset and reset priority**
   - Write nonzero values to `x5` and `x31`. Assert reset between clock edges and check that reads of `x0`, `x5`, and `x31` on both ports return zero without a clock edge.
   - While reset is asserted, attempt a write to `x5` on a rising edge. Deassert reset and check that the representative registers still read zero.
   - Also assert reset at a rising edge with a write enabled and check that reset takes priority.

2. **Asynchronous reads and independent ports**
   - Write distinct values to `x5` and `x31`. With no clock edge, change one read address at a time among `x0`, `x5`, and `x31`.
   - Check that the selected port updates asynchronously and that the other port continues to return the value selected by its unchanged address.

3. **Write data, destination, and preservation**
   - Set distinct values in `x5` and `x31`. Write a new value to `x5` and check that `x5` changes while `x31` retains its prior value; repeat with `x31` as the destination.
   - Use representative data patterns such as `0x00000000`, `0xFFFFFFFF`, `0xAAAAAAAA`, `0x55555555`, and `0x80000001` to check full-width data routing.

4. **Write enable and edge qualification**
   - With known values in `x5` and `x31`, set `rd_write = '0'`, vary `rd_addr` and `rd_data`, and generate rising edges. Check that the representative register values do not change.
   - For a write to `x5`, check that its value remains unchanged before the rising edge, changes after the edge, and remains unchanged when `rd_data` changes without another rising edge.

5. **Hardwired zero**
   - Attempt writes to `x0` with `rd_write = '1'` and representative values including all zeros and all ones.
   - Check that both read ports return zero for `x0` and that the values in `x5` and `x31` remain unchanged.

6. **Post-reset operation**
   - After reset, write a nonzero value to `x5` on a rising edge. Check that both read ports return the written value for `x5`, while `x0` and `x31` return zero.


## alu
# Component semantic contract: alu

## Public interface
```vhdl
entity alu is
    port(
        operand_a : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        operand_b : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        alu_control : in std_logic_vector(3 downto 0);
        result : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        equal : out std_logic;
        signed_less : out std_logic;
        unsigned_less : out std_logic
    );
end alu;
```

## Responsibility
Perform RV32I arithmetic, logic, shifts, and signed and unsigned comparisons selected by an operation control input.

## Timing

`alu` is purely combinational. After input changes propagate, `result`, `equal`, `signed_less`, and `unsigned_less` must reflect the current inputs. There is no clock, stored state, or latency.

## Reset

None. The component has no reset input or reset behavior.

## Behavior

`operand_a` and `operand_b` are 32-bit bit vectors. For binary inputs, `alu_control` selects the operation that determines `result`, as specified below.

The three comparison outputs are independent of `alu_control` and are always computed from the current operands:

- `equal` is `'1'` exactly when `operand_a` and `operand_b` are bit-for-bit equal.
- `signed_less` is `'1'` exactly when `operand_a` is less than `operand_b` interpreted as 32-bit two’s-complement signed integers.
- `unsigned_less` is `'1'` exactly when `operand_a` is less than `operand_b` interpreted as unsigned integers.

These outputs are defined for every binary operand pair, including when `alu_control` is reserved.

## Operations

The `alu_control` encoding is:

| `alu_control` | Operation | `result` |
|---|---|---|
| `0000` | ADD | `(operand_a + operand_b) mod 2^32` |
| `0001` | SUB | `(operand_a - operand_b) mod 2^32` |
| `0010` | AND | Bitwise `operand_a AND operand_b` |
| `0011` | OR | Bitwise `operand_a OR operand_b` |
| `0100` | XOR | Bitwise `operand_a XOR operand_b` |
| `0101` | SLL | `operand_a` shifted logically left by `operand_b[4:0]` places |
| `0110` | SRL | `operand_a` shifted logically right by `operand_b[4:0]` places |
| `0111` | SRA | `operand_a` shifted arithmetically right by `operand_b[4:0]` places, preserving its sign bit |
| `1000` | SLT | `00000000` with bit 0 set to `1` if `signed_less` is `'1'`; otherwise all zero |
| `1001` | SLTU | `00000000` with bit 0 set to `1` if `unsigned_less` is `'1'`; otherwise all zero |
| `1010`–`1111` | Reserved | `00000000` |

For shifts, only the low five bits of `operand_b` determine the shift amount. Vacated bits are zero for SLL and SRL. For SRA, vacated bits are copies of `operand_a[31]`.

## Edge cases

- ADD and SUB wrap modulo `2^32`; overflow does not raise an exception or alter any output other than the arithmetic result.
- A shift amount is always in the range 0–31 because it is taken from `operand_b[4:0]`. In particular, `operand_b` values whose low five bits are zero request a shift by zero, regardless of their other bits.
- Shifting by zero leaves `operand_a` unchanged for SLL, SRL, and SRA.
- SRA of a negative signed operand fills vacated high bits with ones; SRA of a nonnegative operand fills them with zeros.
- SLT and SLTU produce only `0x00000000` or `0x00000001`.
- Reserved selector values produce a zero result. The comparison outputs remain defined from the operands and are not forced to zero by a reserved selector.
- The contract defines behavior for binary inputs. Behavior for inputs containing unknown or high-impedance values is unspecified.

## Test strategy

Run each test by driving all inputs, allowing combinational propagation to settle, then checking all four outputs. Use binary vectors. In each comparison below, change only the stated semantic factor while holding the other inputs fixed.

1. **Selector decoding and operation results.** For each selector in `0000`–`1001`, apply the same asymmetric operands `operand_a = 0x81234567` and `operand_b = 0x10203005`, then check `result` against the operation table. These operands have distinct bits and values so selecting the wrong operand, operation, or shift amount is observable. Change only `alu_control` between cases. For each reserved selector `1010`–`1111`, keep those operands fixed, change only `alu_control`, and require a zero result.

2. **ADD and SUB arithmetic boundaries.** With the selector fixed to ADD, test `(0xFFFFFFFF, 0x00000001) → 0x00000000`, `(0x7FFFFFFF, 0x00000001) → 0x80000000`, and `(0x00000005, 0x00000003) → 0x00000008`. With the selector fixed to SUB, test `(0x00000000, 0x00000001) → 0xFFFFFFFF`, `(0x80000000, 0x00000001) → 0x7FFFFFFF`, and `(0x00000005, 0x00000003) → 0x00000002`. Within each pair of tests, change one operand at a time.

3. **Bitwise transformations.** For AND, OR, and XOR, hold operands at `0xA55A3CC3` and `0x3C969669`, and select each operation in turn. Check the bitwise result exactly. The differing, mixed-bit patterns make the three results distinguishable; change only the selector between cases.

4. **Shift direction and fill behavior.** Hold `operand_a = 0x81234567` and set the shift amount to 4. Check SLL gives `0x12345670`, SRL gives `0x08123456`, and SRA gives `0xF8123456`; change only the selector between cases. Repeat the three operations with `operand_a = 0x71234567` and the same shift amount, checking the corresponding results with zero-fill for right shifts. Change only `operand_a` for that repeat.

5. **Shift amount selection and boundaries.** For each shift selector, hold `operand_a` fixed and test `operand_b` values `0`, `1`, `31`, `32`, and `63`. Check that the effective amounts are respectively `0`, `1`, `31`, `0`, and `31`, including the appropriate shift direction and fill behavior. Change only `operand_b` between cases. Also compare `operand_b = 1` with `operand_b = 0xFFFFFFE1`: the results must match because both have low five bits equal to one; change only the upper bits of `operand_b`.

6. **Signed comparison result and flag.** With SLT selected, test `(0x80000000, 0x7FFFFFFF)` and its operand-reversed pair; require `signed_less` and the SLT result to change from true to false. Test `(0xFFFFFFFF, 0x00000000)` and its reversed pair to distinguish signed interpretation from unsigned interpretation. Test equal operands to require `signed_less = 0` and SLT result zero. Change only the operand order or the single operand needed for each pair.

7. **Unsigned comparison result and flag.** With SLTU selected, test `(0xFFFFFFFF, 0x00000000)` and its operand-reversed pair; require `unsigned_less` and the SLTU result to change from false to true. Test `(0x80000000, 0x7FFFFFFF)` and its reversed pair to distinguish unsigned from signed interpretation. Test equal operands to require `unsigned_less = 0` and SLTU result zero. Change only the operand order or the single operand needed for each pair.

8. **Equality flag.** Apply equal operands such as `(0xA55A3CC3, 0xA55A3CC3)` and require `equal = 1`; change one operand by one bit and require `equal = 0`. Repeat with several operand patterns, including zero and `0xFFFFFFFF`. Change only one operand between equal and unequal cases.

9. **Flag independence from operation selection.** For each of these operand pairs—equal operands, signed-less-only operands `(0xFFFFFFFF, 0x00000000)`, unsigned-less-only operands `(0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000)`, and operands with neither strict less-than relation `(0x00000001, 0x00000001)`—hold both operands fixed and apply every selector from `0000` through `1111`. Require `equal`, `signed_less`, and `unsigned_less` to remain equal to their operand-defined values for every selector. Change only `alu_control` within each pair.


## decoder
# Component semantic contract: decoder

## Public interface
```vhdl
entity decoder is
    port(
        instr : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        reg_write : out std_logic;
        mem_write : out std_logic;
        alu_src_a_pc : out std_logic;
        alu_src_b_imm : out std_logic;
        alu_control : out std_logic_vector(3 downto 0);
        branch_enable : out std_logic;
        jump : out std_logic;
        jalr : out std_logic;
        wb_select : out std_logic_vector(1 downto 0)
    );
end decoder;
```

## Responsibility
Decode RV32I instruction opcode and function fields into register-write, memory-write, operand-source, ALU-operation, branch, jump, and writeback-selection controls.

## Timing

`decoder` is purely combinational. After `instr` changes, every output shall settle to the value specified below without requiring a clock edge. The decoder has no state, handshake, or latency.

## Reset

None. The decoder has no reset input. Its outputs are determined solely by `instr`.

## Behavior

`instr` is a 32-bit RV32I instruction. The decoder uses `instr[6:0]` as the opcode, `instr[14:12]` as `funct3`, and, where specified, `instr[31:25]` as `funct7`.

For every recognized instruction encoding, outputs shall match the instruction-class definitions below. For any unsupported opcode or unsupported function encoding, the instruction shall have no architectural side effects: `reg_write`, `mem_write`, `branch_enable`, `jump`, and `jalr` shall be `'0'`; `alu_src_a_pc` and `alu_src_b_imm` shall be `'0'`; `alu_control` shall be `"0000"`; and `wb_select` shall be `"00"`.

For valid instructions, `reg_write` indicates that the instruction produces a register result. It is asserted for register-writing instruction classes even when `rd` is `x0`; suppression of writes to `x0` is the responsibility of the register-file component. `mem_write` is asserted only for valid stores. `branch_enable` is asserted only for valid conditional branches. `jump` is asserted for `JAL` and `JALR`; `jalr` is asserted only for `JALR`.

`alu_src_a_pc` selects the PC as ALU operand A when `'1'`, and `rs1` otherwise. `alu_src_b_imm` selects the instruction’s applicable immediate as ALU operand B when `'1'`, and `rs2` otherwise. For instructions whose ALU operands do not affect their architectural result, the source controls and ALU control are nevertheless specified below.

Valid instruction classes and their controls:

| Instruction class | `reg_write` | `mem_write` | `alu_src_a_pc` | `alu_src_b_imm` | `branch_enable` | `jump` | `jalr` | `wb_select` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| OP (`0x33`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| OP-IMM (`0x13`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| Loads (`0x03`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"01"` |
| Stores (`0x23`) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| Conditional branches (`0x63`) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| LUI (`0x37`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| AUIPC (`0x17`) | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| JAL (`0x6F`) | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | `"10"` |
| JALR (`0x67`, `funct3="000"`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | `"10"` |

The ALU control and operand meaning for each valid class are specified in `Operations`. For JAL and JALR, the ALU control is `"0000"`; jump-target generation is not selected by `alu_control`.

## Operations

`alu_control` is a four-bit selector. Its meaning for non-branch instructions is:

| `alu_control` | Operation |
|---|---|
| `"0000"` | ADD |
| `"0001"` | SUB |
| `"0010"` | SLL |
| `"0011"` | SLT (signed) |
| `"0100"` | SLTU (unsigned) |
| `"0101"` | XOR |
| `"0110"` | SRL |
| `"0111"` | SRA |
| `"1000"` | OR |
| `"1001"` | AND |
| `"1010"` | PASS_B: the result is operand B |
| `"1011"`–`"1111"` | Not selected for non-branch instructions |

When `branch_enable='1'`, `alu_control` instead selects the branch condition:

| `alu_control` | Branch condition |
|---|---|
| `"0000"` | BEQ |
| `"0001"` | BNE |
| `"0010"` | BLT (signed) |
| `"0011"` | BGE (signed) |
| `"0100"` | BLTU (unsigned) |
| `"0101"` | BGEU (unsigned) |

The branch-specific meanings apply only when `branch_enable='1'`.

`wb_select` is a two-bit selector:

| `wb_select` | Writeback source |
|---|---|
| `"00"` | ALU result |
| `"01"` | Data-memory read result |
| `"10"` | `PC + 4` |
| `"11"` | Reserved; never selected by a valid instruction |

Opcode and function decoding:

| Opcode | Required function encoding | `alu_control` | Additional behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="000"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="000"`, `funct7="0100000"` | `"0001"` SUB | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="001"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0010"` SLL | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="010"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0011"` SLT | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="011"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0100"` SLTU | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="100"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0101"` XOR | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="101"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0110"` SRL | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="101"`, `funct7="0100000"` | `"0111"` SRA | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="110"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"1000"` OR | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="111"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"1001"` AND | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="000"` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="001"`, `instr[31:25]="0000000"` | `"0010"` SLL | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="010"` | `"0011"` SLT | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="011"` | `"0100"` SLTU | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="100"` | `"0101"` XOR | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="101"`, `instr[31:25]="0000000"` | `"0110"` SRL | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="101"`, `instr[31:25]="0100000"` | `"0111"` SRA | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="110"` | `"1000"` OR | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="111"` | `"1001"` AND | |
| `0x03` Load | `funct3` in `"000"`, `"001"`, `"010"`, `"100"`, `"101"` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x23` Store | `funct3` in `"000"`, `"001"`, `"010"` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="000"` | `"0000"` BEQ | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="001"` | `"0001"` BNE | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="100"` | `"0010"` BLT | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="101"` | `"0011"` BGE | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="110"` | `"0100"` BLTU | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="111"` | `"0101"` BGEU | |
| `0x37` LUI | Any `funct3` and `funct7` | `"1010"` PASS_B | |
| `0x17` AUIPC | Any `funct3` and `funct7` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x6F` JAL | Any `funct3` and `funct7` | `"0000"` | |
| `0x67` JALR | `funct3="000"` | `"0000"` ADD | |

For OP and OP-IMM, all function encodings not listed above are unsupported. For loads, stores, branches, and JALR, function encodings not listed above are unsupported. LUI, AUIPC, and JAL do not have function-field restrictions in this contract.

## Edge cases

- OP encodings are valid only for the exact `funct7` values shown. In particular, the SUB and SRA encodings are distinct from their ADD and SRL counterparts; all other OP `funct7` combinations are unsupported.
- SLLI, SRLI, and SRAI are valid only for the exact upper-bit patterns shown. Their shift amount is not decoded as a selector by this component.
- For non-shift OP-IMM instructions, `instr[31:25]` does not restrict validity or change the selected operation.
- `rd`, `rs1`, `rs2`, and immediate bits do not change the controls except where explicitly used as function bits above.
- Any unsupported function combination, including an otherwise recognized opcode with an invalid `funct3` or required `funct7`, produces the no-side-effect outputs defined in `Behavior`.
- All outputs have defined values for every possible 32-bit `instr`; there are no don’t-care outputs.

## Test strategy

Use a combinational Cocotb test that drives a complete 32-bit instruction, allows outputs to settle, and checks every output against the contract. Run each case without a clock or reset stimulus.

1. **Opcode-class controls and writeback selection:** For each valid class in the `Behavior` table, drive a canonical instruction and check the complete output tuple, including `reg_write`, `mem_write`, both operand selectors, branch/jump controls, `alu_control`, and `wb_select`. Use different values for `rd`, `rs1`, `rs2`, and immediate fields between cases so field changes cannot accidentally conceal opcode-class selection errors. Include `rd=x0` for at least one register-writing instruction and require `reg_write='1'`.

2. **OP operations:** Exercise every valid OP `funct3`/`funct7` pair in `Operations`. For each case, hold opcode and all fields other than the function selector constant, vary only the relevant `funct3` or `funct7`, and check the exact `alu_control` and full output tuple. Use distinct `funct3` and `funct7` values to distinguish each operation. Also exercise invalid `funct7` values for each relevant OP `funct3`, including the alternate `funct7` for ADD/SUB, SRL/SRA, and at least one unsupported pattern for every other `funct3`; require the unsupported-instruction outputs.

3. **OP-IMM operations and function restrictions:** Exercise every valid OP-IMM row, changing only `funct3` or, for shift operations, only `instr[31:25]` between related cases. Check the exact ALU selector and full tuple. For SLLI, SRLI, and SRAI, test both permitted and disallowed upper-bit patterns. For each non-shift `funct3`, vary `instr[31:25]` while holding the other fields fixed and require that controls remain unchanged.

4. **Loads and stores:** Exercise each valid load and store `funct3` independently, checking all outputs and confirming that only loads assert `reg_write` and select `"01"`, while only stores assert `mem_write`. Vary `rd`, `rs1`, `rs2`, and immediate fields independently while keeping opcode and `funct3` fixed; require that controls remain unchanged. Test every unsupported load/store `funct3` and require the no-side-effect outputs.

5. **Branches:** Exercise all six valid branch `funct3` values, varying only `funct3` between cases. Check `branch_enable`, the branch-specific `alu_control`, and all other outputs. Use distinct function values to ensure each condition is selected correctly. Test unsupported branch `funct3` values and require the no-side-effect outputs.

6. **Unrestricted instruction fields:** For LUI, AUIPC, and JAL, vary `funct3` and `funct7` while holding the opcode and other fields fixed; require their controls to remain unchanged. For non-shift OP-IMM operations, vary `instr[31:25]` in the same manner. In each case, separately vary register-index and immediate bits and confirm they do not alter the decoded controls.

7. **JALR restriction and jump controls:** Check JAL and valid JALR as separate cases, requiring `jump='1'`, the specified `jalr` value, and `"10"` writeback selection. Vary JALR `funct3` across all values; require the valid encoding to match the JALR row and every other value to produce the no-side-effect outputs.

8. **Unknown opcodes and invalid encodings:** Drive representative unrecognized opcode values and every invalid function combination required above. For each, check the entire no-side-effect output tuple, not only the side-effect flags.

9. **Combinational response:** Apply consecutive instructions from different classes without any intervening clock. After each input change, require outputs to match that instruction’s expected tuple. Include transitions between valid and unsupported instructions and between classes with different writeback and control selections to detect stale output values.


## cpu
# Component semantic contract: cpu

## Public interface
```vhdl
entity cpu is
    port(
        clk : in std_logic;
        rst : in std_logic;
        instr_addr : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        instr_data : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        data_addr : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        data_write : out std_logic;
        data_width : out std_logic_vector(1 downto 0);
        data_write_data : out std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        data_read_data : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0)
    );
end cpu;
```

## Responsibility
Implement the RV32I single-cycle top level: maintain the PC, instantiate the register file, decoder, ALU, and immediate generator, select branch and jump targets, perform load extraction and extension, and drive the instruction and data buses exactly as specified.

## Timing

- `cpu` is an RV32I single-cycle processor. `instr_addr` exposes the byte address of the current instruction, and `instr_data` is the asynchronous instruction word at that address.
- With `rst = '0'`, each rising edge of `clk` completes the current instruction: any register write and any external store take effect on that edge, and the PC advances to the instruction’s next address.
- Decode, register reads, effective-address generation, bus outputs, load extraction, writeback selection, branch decisions, and next-PC selection are combinational. They respond to current inputs without waiting for a clock edge.
- `data_read_data` is the asynchronous little-endian word based at `data_addr & 0xFFFFFFFC`. A load uses its value when the load completes at the rising edge.
- The fixed decomposition is mandatory: `cpu` instantiates exactly one each of `immediate_generator`, `register_file`, `alu`, and `decoder`, and does not reimplement their behavior. These dependencies are combinational except for the register file, which has the state and edge behavior specified by its own contract.

## Reset

- `rst` is active high and asynchronous.
- While `rst = '1'`, `instr_addr` is `0x00000000`, and architectural registers read as zero. Reset does not require a clock edge.
- A rising edge while reset is asserted does not execute an instruction, update the PC, write a register, or cause an external data-memory write. `data_write` is `'0'` throughout reset.
- Deasserting reset does not itself advance the PC or change register contents. Execution resumes from address zero at the next rising edge.

## Behavior

- The public interface is fixed to the `cpu` entity and ports in the accompanying entity declaration. The CPU must not add public ports, generics, or external memory instances.
- The PC is a 32-bit byte address. For each executed instruction, its next value is selected in this order:
  1. `JAL` or valid `JALR`: use the corresponding jump target.
  2. A taken conditional branch: use the branch target.
  3. Otherwise: use `PC + 4`.
  
  PC arithmetic wraps modulo \(2^{32}\). `JAL x0, 0` leaves the PC unchanged on each rising edge.
- `JAL` writes `PC + 4` to `rd` and targets `PC + imm_j`. Valid `JALR` writes `PC + 4` to `rd` and targets `(rs1 + imm_i) & 0xFFFFFFFE`. A branch target is `PC + imm_b`.
- The register file has 32 architectural 32-bit registers. `x0` always reads as zero, and writes to `x0` have no effect. Register reads are asynchronous; a valid write takes effect on the rising edge completing the instruction.
- `data_addr` is the effective byte address for loads and stores: `rs1 + imm_i` for loads and `rs1 + imm_s` for stores. Its low bits are not masked.
- For loads and stores, `data_width` is `"00"` for byte, `"01"` for halfword, and `"10"` for word. `"11"` is not selected by a valid load or store.
- For loads, `data_read_data` is interpreted as a little-endian word based at `data_addr & 0xFFFFFFFC`. The address low bits select the byte or halfword. `LB` and `LH` sign-extend; `LBU` and `LHU` zero-extend; `LW` uses the full word.
- For valid stores, `data_write` is `'1'` during the store instruction cycle, `data_write_data` is the unshifted `rs2` value, and `data_width` identifies which low 8, 16, or 32 bits are written. The external memory commits the write on the rising edge. For every non-store instruction, and during reset, `data_write` is `'0'`.
- `data_addr`, `data_width`, and `data_write_data` have no architectural meaning when `data_write = '0'` and the current instruction is not a load. For loads, `data_addr` and `data_width` identify the effective address and access size.
- Unsupported opcodes and unsupported function encodings have no architectural side effects: they do not write a register or memory, do not branch or jump, and advance the PC by four. Their data-bus outputs other than `data_write = '0'` have no architectural meaning.

## Operations

Instruction fields are `opcode = instr[6:0]`, `rd = instr[11:7]`, `funct3 = instr[14:12]`, `rs1 = instr[19:15]`, `rs2 = instr[24:20]`, and `funct7 = instr[31:25]`. The immediate generator supplies all five immediates concurrently:
- `imm_i = sext(instr[31:20])`
- `imm_s = sext(instr[31:25] || instr[11:7])`
- `imm_b = sext(instr[31] || instr[7] || instr[30:25] || instr[11:8] || 0)`
- `imm_u = instr[31:12] || 12'b0`
- `imm_j = sext(instr[31] || instr[19:12] || instr[20] || instr[30:21] || 0)`

Here `sext` is sign extension to 32 bits. Immediate selection is by instruction class; the immediate generator itself has no selector.

| Instruction | Opcode | Valid function encoding | Architectural operation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `LUI` | `0x37` | Any `funct3`, `funct7` | `rd = U` |
| `AUIPC` | `0x17` | Any `funct3`, `funct7` | `rd = PC + U` |
| `JAL` | `0x6F` | Any `funct3`, `funct7` | `rd = PC + 4`; jump to `PC + J` |
| `JALR` | `0x67` | `funct3 = 000` | `rd = PC + 4`; jump to `(rs1 + I) & 0xFFFFFFFE` |
| `BEQ` | `0x63` | `funct3 = 000` | Branch if `rs1 == rs2` |
| `BNE` | `0x63` | `funct3 = 001` | Branch if `rs1 != rs2` |
| `BLT` | `0x63` | `funct3 = 100` | Branch if signed `rs1 < rs2` |
| `BGE` | `0x63` | `funct3 = 101` | Branch if signed `rs1 >= rs2` |
| `BLTU` | `0x63` | `funct3 = 110` | Branch if unsigned `rs1 < rs2` |
| `BGEU` | `0x63` | `funct3 = 111` | Branch if unsigned `rs1 >= rs2` |
| `LB` | `0x03` | `funct3 = 000` | Load signed byte |
| `LH` | `0x03` | `funct3 = 001` | Load signed halfword |
| `LW` | `0x03` | `funct3 = 010` | Load word |
| `LBU` | `0x03` | `funct3 = 100` | Load unsigned byte |
| `LHU` | `0x03` | `funct3 = 101` | Load unsigned halfword |
| `SB` | `0x23` | `funct3 = 000` | Store low byte of `rs2` |
| `SH` | `0x23` | `funct3 = 001` | Store low halfword of `rs2` |
| `SW` | `0x23` | `funct3 = 010` | Store `rs2` word |
| `ADD` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 000`, `funct7 = 0000000` | `rd = rs1 + rs2` |
| `SUB` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 000`, `funct7 = 0100000` | `rd = rs1 - rs2` |
| `SLL` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 001`, `funct7 = 0000000` | `rd = rs1 << rs2[4:0]` |
| `SLT` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 010`, `funct7 = 0000000` | `rd = 1` iff signed `rs1 < rs2` |
| `SLTU` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 011`, `funct7 = 0000000` | `rd = 1` iff unsigned `rs1 < rs2` |
| `XOR` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 100`, `funct7 = 0000000` | `rd = rs1 XOR rs2` |
| `SRL` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 101`, `funct7 = 0000000` | Logical right shift by `rs2[4:0]` |
| `SRA` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 101`, `funct7 = 0100000` | Arithmetic right shift by `rs2[4:0]` |
| `OR` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 110`, `funct7 = 0000000` | `rd = rs1 OR rs2` |
| `AND` | `0x33` | `funct3 = 111`, `funct7 = 0000000` | `rd = rs1 AND rs2` |
| `ADDI` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 000` | `rd = rs1 + I` |
| `SLLI` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 001`, `instr[31:25] = 0000000` | `rd = rs1 << instr[24:20]` |
| `SLTI` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 010` | `rd = 1` iff signed `rs1 < I` |
| `SLTIU` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 011` | `rd = 1` iff unsigned `rs1 < I` |
| `XORI` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 100` | `rd = rs1 XOR I` |
| `SRLI` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 101`, `instr[31:25] = 0000000` | Logical right shift by `instr[24:20]` |
| `SRAI` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 101`, `instr[31:25] = 0100000` | Arithmetic right shift by `instr[24:20]` |
| `ORI` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 110` | `rd = rs1 OR I` |
| `ANDI` | `0x13` | `funct3 = 111` | `rd = rs1 AND I` |

The selector encodings of `decoder` and `alu` are private to those dependencies and are not required to be numerically identical. The parent CPU shall perform the following explicit adaptation for non-branch ALU operations. The left column is the decoder’s `alu_control`; the right column is the `alu_control` presented to the ALU:

| Decoder selector | Meaning | ALU selector |
|---|---|---|
| `"0000"` | ADD | `"0000"` |
| `"0001"` | SUB | `"0001"` |
| `"0010"` | SLL | `"0101"` |
| `"0011"` | signed SLT | `"1000"` |
| `"0100"` | unsigned SLTU | `"1001"` |
| `"0101"` | XOR | `"0100"` |
| `"0110"` | SRL | `"0110"` |
| `"0111"` | SRA | `"0111"` |
| `"1000"` | OR | `"0011"` |
| `"1001"` | AND | `"0010"` |
| `"1010"` | PASS_B for LUI | Do not rely on an ALU PASS_B operation; select `imm_u` directly as the LUI writeback value |

For branches, the decoder’s branch selector has these meanings: `"0000"` BEQ, `"0001"` BNE, `"0010"` BLT, `"0011"` BGE, `"0100"` BLTU, and `"0101"` BGEU. The CPU uses the ALU’s `equal`, `signed_less`, and `unsigned_less` outputs to evaluate the selected condition. The branch selector is not sent to the ALU as a non-branch operation selector. `alu` comparison outputs are defined independently of its operation selector.

The decoder’s `alu_src_a_pc` and `alu_src_b_imm` controls select the indicated source class, but do not themselves choose an immediate format. The CPU supplies the applicable operand: `imm_i` for OP-IMM and loads, `imm_s` for stores, and `imm_u` for LUI and AUIPC. AUIPC uses PC and `imm_u`; LUI writes `imm_u` directly. Branch, jump-target, and link-value generation follow the architectural rules above.

## Edge cases

- All architectural integer results, effective addresses, PC additions, and PC-relative targets wrap modulo \(2^{32}\); arithmetic overflow raises no exception.
- Shift amounts use only the low five bits of the relevant source. `SRA` and `SRAI` replicate the source sign bit; logical shifts fill vacated bits with zero.
- `SLT`, `SLTU`, `SLTI`, and `SLTIU` produce exactly zero or one.
- `JALR` clears target bit zero after adding its immediate. `JAL` and branch immediates have an implicit zero at bit zero.
- `JAL x0, 0` is a valid self-loop and keeps `instr_addr` unchanged on successive rising edges.
- The external data-memory interface assumes naturally aligned accesses. Behavior for misaligned halfword or word accesses is unspecified.
- Inputs are defined for binary `std_logic` values. Behavior for unknown or high-impedance values is unspecified.
- No instruction can simultaneously be a jump and a conditional branch: their opcodes are distinct. The specified next-PC ordering therefore does not create a reachable overlap case.

## Test strategy

Use executable Cocotb tests with a software reference model for the PC, architectural register values, instruction behavior, and external memory. Tests observe only the CPU’s public ports: they must not require direct reads of internal registers or selectors. Drive inputs, allow combinational propagation to settle, check bus outputs before the active edge, then apply the rising edge and check `instr_addr` and any externally observable effects. Use binary inputs and distinct values so incorrect sources, slices, or selections are observable.

Observe register effects through later public behavior rather than by inspecting register state: for example, store a register value to external memory and check the committed memory contents, or use the value in a branch and check the resulting `instr_addr`. `x0` behavior can likewise be checked by using it as a later store source or branch operand.

1. **Fetch, sequencing, and edge qualification**
   - Assert reset asynchronously and require `instr_addr = 0`; deassert reset without a clock and require it remains zero.
   - Execute sequential instructions with distinguishable effects. Before each rising edge, require `instr_addr` to equal the current PC; after the edge, require the expected next PC.
   - Hold inputs constant while the clock is low and verify the PC does not advance. Verify that an instruction’s architectural effects occur only at the rising edge.

2. **Register effects and writeback routing**
   - Initialize registers through executed instructions using distinct, nonzero values. Verify results through later stores or branches; do not check internal register state directly.
   - Exercise writeback from OP, OP-IMM, LUI, AUIPC, loads, JAL, and JALR. For each class, use the resulting register value in a later public operation, such as a store to a known address.
   - Repeat representative writes with `rd = x0`; verify that later reads through stores or branches still observe zero.
   - Reset after populating registers, then use those registers in later instructions to verify reset-cleared values through public behavior. Keep reset asserted across a rising edge and verify no instruction side effect occurs.

3. **Instruction decoding and ALU transformations**
   - Execute every valid OP and OP-IMM encoding in **Operations**, using asymmetric source values such as `0x81234567` and `0x10203005`. Verify results through subsequent stores or branches.
   - Test ADD/ADDI and SUB wraparound and signed-boundary operands, including `0xFFFFFFFF + 1`, `0x7FFFFFFF + 1`, and `0 - 1`.
   - For SLL/SLLI/SRL/SRLI/SRA/SRAI, test amounts 0, 1, and 31, and compare source amounts with differing upper bits but matching low five bits. Use negative and nonnegative operands to distinguish shift fill.
   - For signed and unsigned comparisons, use pairs such as `0xFFFFFFFF` and `0x00000000`, and test equality. Verify results are exactly zero or one through later public behavior.
   - For XOR, OR, and AND, use mixed bit patterns and verify exact results through a store or a branch that distinguishes the result.
   - Exercise unsupported OP, OP-IMM, load, store, branch, and JALR function encodings. Require no register or memory write, no redirect, and sequential PC advance. Also test representative unsupported opcodes.

4. **Immediate selection and transformations**
   - Construct I-, S-, B-, U-, and J-format instructions with distinguishable nonzero patterns in their immediate slices. Verify the effective address, stored or loaded value, ALU result, or target uses the specified format and bit ordering.
   - Test positive and negative I, S, B, and J immediates. For each format, vary only the sign bit and verify the sign-extension effect through a public address or control-flow result.
   - For U-type values, verify the low 12 result bits are zero and the upper 20 bits match the instruction, using a later store or branch to expose the result.
   - Test branch and jump offsets with nonzero encoded bits and verify the implicit low zero bit and target calculation.

5. **Branches and control flow**
   - Test BEQ and BNE with equal and unequal values. Test BLT, BGE, BLTU, and BGEU with both outcomes, including operand pairs such as `0xFFFFFFFF` and `0x00000000` that distinguish signed from unsigned comparisons.
   - For each condition, check taken and not-taken next PCs. Test forward and backward targets and verify a not-taken branch uses `PC + 4`.
   - Test JAL and valid JALR redirects separately, and test that invalid JALR function encodings do not redirect. A jump-versus-taken-branch priority overlap test is not applicable: no single instruction can be both classes.
   - Execute `JAL x0, 0` repeatedly and require `instr_addr` to remain at the same address on every edge.

6. **Jump targets and link values**
   - For JAL, use positive and negative offsets and a nonzero `rd`; verify the target through `instr_addr` and the link value through a later store or branch. Vary the offset and destination in separate comparisons.
   - For JALR, use distinct `rs1` values and positive and negative I immediates; verify the summed target with bit zero cleared and verify `PC + 4` through a later public operation.
   - Exercise JALR `funct3 = 000` and require all other `funct3` values to have no link write or PC redirect.

7. **Load address, width, extraction, and extension**
   - For LB, LBU, LH, LHU, and LW, drive a base and immediate that produce a distinguishable effective byte address. Check that `data_addr` is unmasked and `data_width` is correct.
   - Use a read word with four distinct bytes, such as `0xD3A57C19`. Test byte offsets 0, 1, 2, and 3, including bytes with the high bit set and clear; verify selected values and sign or zero extension through a later store or branch.
   - Test halfword offsets 0 and 2 with distinct lower and upper halfwords, including signed-positive and signed-negative values. Verify LH sign extension and LHU zero extension. For LW, verify all 32 bits are preserved.
   - Change only `data_read_data` between otherwise identical load executions and verify the loaded value follows the current memory input. Require loads never to assert `data_write`.

8. **Store routing, payload, and suppression**
   - For SB, SH, and SW, use distinct base, immediate, and `rs2` patterns. Check the unmasked effective byte address, `data_write = '1'`, correct width, and unshifted `rs2` on `data_write_data`. Verify the external memory commits the appropriate low 8, 16, or 32 bits only at the rising edge.
   - Change `rs2` before the edge and require the bus payload to track it; change it after the edge without another edge and verify no second store occurs.
   - For every non-store class, including unsupported instructions, require `data_write = '0'`. While reset is asserted, require `data_write = '0'` even if `instr_data` encodes a store.

9. **Reset and post-reset execution**
   - Assert reset between clock edges after instructions have changed the PC and registers. Require `instr_addr` to become zero immediately and remain zero while reset is held.
   - Keep reset asserted across a rising edge with inputs that would otherwise request register and memory writes. Verify no store occurs, and use subsequent public behavior after reset to verify registers read as zero.
   - Deassert reset without a clock and verify state does not advance until the next rising edge. Then execute a register-writing instruction and a store to confirm normal operation resumes from address zero.

+# RV32M Implementation Reference
+# RV32M — referência de implementação
+
+Fonte: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA, extensão "M" para multiplicação e divisão
+inteiras, versão 2.0 (RISC-V International, CC-BY-4.0).
+
+Este arquivo só vale quando `specs/cpu.md` declara **RV32IM**. Ele completa
+`riscv-rv32i.md`, que continua valendo inteiro: RV32IM = RV32I + M. Com
+**RV32I** este arquivo não vai para a IA e a CPU não implementa nenhuma
+instrução abaixo.
+
+## Codificação
+
+Todas as instruções M são R-type, com `opcode = 0110011` (`0x33`, o mesmo do
+OP do RV32I) e `funct7 = 0000001` (`0x01`). O `funct7` é o que separa M de
+ADD/SUB/shifts/lógica: no RV32I ele vale `0x00` ou `0x20`.
+
+| Instrução | `funct3` | `funct7` | Resultado em `rd` |
+|---|---:|---:|---|
+| MUL | `0x0` | `0x01` | 32 bits baixos de `rs1 × rs2` |
+| MULH | `0x1` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `signed(rs1) × signed(rs2)` |
+| MULHSU | `0x2` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `signed(rs1) × unsigned(rs2)` |
+| MULHU | `0x3` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `unsigned(rs1) × unsigned(rs2)` |
+| DIV | `0x4` | `0x01` | quociente signed, arredondado para zero |
+| DIVU | `0x5` | `0x01` | quociente unsigned |
+| REM | `0x6` | `0x01` | resto signed; o sinal é o do dividendo (`rs1`) |
+| REMU | `0x7` | `0x01` | resto unsigned |
+
+## Regras gerais
+
+- O produto completo tem 64 bits. MUL devolve os bits `[31:0]` e é o mesmo
+  para operandos signed ou unsigned. MULH, MULHSU e MULHU devolvem os bits
+  `[63:32]`.
+- MULHSU trata `rs1` como signed e `rs2` como unsigned. Não troque a ordem.
+- Divisão e resto truncam para zero: `-7 / 2 = -3` e `-7 rem 2 = -1`.
+- Nenhuma instrução M gera exceção, trap ou estado extra. `rd = x0` continua
+  sendo ignorado.
+- No contrato monociclo de `specs/cpu.md`, uma instrução completa por borda de
+  subida: o resultado de MUL e DIV precisa estar pronto no mesmo ciclo.
+
+## Casos especiais obrigatórios
+
+A divisão por zero e o overflow têm resultado definido pela ISA. A CPU deve
+produzir exatamente estes valores (`x` é o dividendo `rs1`):
+
+| Caso | DIV | DIVU | REM | REMU |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| divisor = 0 | `-1` (`0xFFFFFFFF`) | `2^32 - 1` (`0xFFFFFFFF`) | `x` | `x` |
+| overflow: `x = -2^31` (`0x80000000`) e divisor = `-1` | `-2^31` (`0x80000000`) | (não se aplica) | `0` | (não se aplica) |
+
+## Exemplos para conferir
+
+| Instrução | `rs1` | `rs2` | `rd` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| MUL | `0x00000007` | `0xFFFFFFFD` (-3) | `0xFFFFFFEB` (-21) |
+| MULH | `0x80000000` | `0x80000000` | `0x40000000` |
+| MULHSU | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) | `0xFFFFFFFF` | `0xFFFFFFFF` |
+| MULHU | `0xFFFFFFFF` | `0xFFFFFFFF` | `0xFFFFFFFE` |
+| DIV | `0xFFFFFFF9` (-7) | `0x00000002` | `0xFFFFFFFD` (-3) |
+| DIVU | `0xFFFFFFF9` | `0x00000002` | `0x7FFFFFFC` |
+| REM | `0xFFFFFFF9` (-7) | `0x00000002` | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) |
+| REMU | `0xFFFFFFF9` | `0x00000002` | `0x00000001` |
+| DIV | `0x00000005` | `0x00000000` | `0xFFFFFFFF` |
+| REM | `0x00000005` | `0x00000000` | `0x00000005` |
+| DIV | `0x80000000` | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) | `0x80000000` |
+| REM | `0x80000000` | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) | `0x00000000` |
+
+## Notas para VHDL (`numeric_std`)
+
+- `signed(a) * signed(b)` com operandos de 32 bits dá 64 bits. Para MULHSU,
+  estenda `rs1` com sinal e `rs2` com zero até 33 bits, multiplique como
+  `signed` (66 bits) e pegue os bits `[63:32]`.
+- `/` e `rem` de `numeric_std` truncam para zero e dão ao resto o sinal do
+  dividendo, como a ISA. Mas dividir por zero em VHDL para a simulação com
+  erro: trate divisor zero e o overflow **antes** de calcular, com as saídas
+  da tabela de casos especiais.
+

Current contract:
# Component semantic contract: decoder

## Public interface
```vhdl
entity decoder is
    port(
        instr : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        reg_write : out std_logic;
        mem_write : out std_logic;
        alu_src_a_pc : out std_logic;
        alu_src_b_imm : out std_logic;
        alu_control : out std_logic_vector(3 downto 0);
        branch_enable : out std_logic;
        jump : out std_logic;
        jalr : out std_logic;
        wb_select : out std_logic_vector(1 downto 0)
    );
end decoder;
```

## Responsibility
Decode RV32I instruction opcode and function fields into register-write, memory-write, operand-source, ALU-operation, branch, jump, and writeback-selection controls.

## Timing

`decoder` is purely combinational. After `instr` changes, every output shall settle to the value specified below without requiring a clock edge. The decoder has no state, handshake, or latency.

## Reset

None. The decoder has no reset input. Its outputs are determined solely by `instr`.

## Behavior

`instr` is a 32-bit RV32I instruction. The decoder uses `instr[6:0]` as the opcode, `instr[14:12]` as `funct3`, and, where specified, `instr[31:25]` as `funct7`.

For every recognized instruction encoding, outputs shall match the instruction-class definitions below. For any unsupported opcode or unsupported function encoding, the instruction shall have no architectural side effects: `reg_write`, `mem_write`, `branch_enable`, `jump`, and `jalr` shall be `'0'`; `alu_src_a_pc` and `alu_src_b_imm` shall be `'0'`; `alu_control` shall be `"0000"`; and `wb_select` shall be `"00"`.

For valid instructions, `reg_write` indicates that the instruction produces a register result. It is asserted for register-writing instruction classes even when `rd` is `x0`; suppression of writes to `x0` is the responsibility of the register-file component. `mem_write` is asserted only for valid stores. `branch_enable` is asserted only for valid conditional branches. `jump` is asserted for `JAL` and `JALR`; `jalr` is asserted only for `JALR`.

`alu_src_a_pc` selects the PC as ALU operand A when `'1'`, and `rs1` otherwise. `alu_src_b_imm` selects the instruction’s applicable immediate as ALU operand B when `'1'`, and `rs2` otherwise. For instructions whose ALU operands do not affect their architectural result, the source controls and ALU control are nevertheless specified below.

Valid instruction classes and their controls:

| Instruction class | `reg_write` | `mem_write` | `alu_src_a_pc` | `alu_src_b_imm` | `branch_enable` | `jump` | `jalr` | `wb_select` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| OP (`0x33`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| OP-IMM (`0x13`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| Loads (`0x03`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"01"` |
| Stores (`0x23`) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| Conditional branches (`0x63`) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| LUI (`0x37`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| AUIPC (`0x17`) | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| JAL (`0x6F`) | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | `"10"` |
| JALR (`0x67`, `funct3="000"`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | `"10"` |

The ALU control and operand meaning for each valid class are specified in `Operations`. For JAL and JALR, the ALU control is `"0000"`; jump-target generation is not selected by `alu_control`.

## Operations

`alu_control` is a four-bit selector. Its meaning for non-branch instructions is:

| `alu_control` | Operation |
|---|---|
| `"0000"` | ADD |
| `"0001"` | SUB |
| `"0010"` | SLL |
| `"0011"` | SLT (signed) |
| `"0100"` | SLTU (unsigned) |
| `"0101"` | XOR |
| `"0110"` | SRL |
| `"0111"` | SRA |
| `"1000"` | OR |
| `"1001"` | AND |
| `"1010"` | PASS_B: the result is operand B |
| `"1011"`–`"1111"` | Not selected for non-branch instructions |

When `branch_enable='1'`, `alu_control` instead selects the branch condition:

| `alu_control` | Branch condition |
|---|---|
| `"0000"` | BEQ |
| `"0001"` | BNE |
| `"0010"` | BLT (signed) |
| `"0011"` | BGE (signed) |
| `"0100"` | BLTU (unsigned) |
| `"0101"` | BGEU (unsigned) |

The branch-specific meanings apply only when `branch_enable='1'`.

`wb_select` is a two-bit selector:

| `wb_select` | Writeback source |
|---|---|
| `"00"` | ALU result |
| `"01"` | Data-memory read result |
| `"10"` | `PC + 4` |
| `"11"` | Reserved; never selected by a valid instruction |

Opcode and function decoding:

| Opcode | Required function encoding | `alu_control` | Additional behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="000"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="000"`, `funct7="0100000"` | `"0001"` SUB | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="001"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0010"` SLL | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="010"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0011"` SLT | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="011"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0100"` SLTU | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="100"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0101"` XOR | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="101"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"0110"` SRL | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="101"`, `funct7="0100000"` | `"0111"` SRA | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="110"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"1000"` OR | |
| `0x33` OP | `funct3="111"`, `funct7="0000000"` | `"1001"` AND | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="000"` | `"0000"` ADD | |

# Component semantic contract: decoder

## Public interface
```vhdl
entity decoder is
    port(
        instr : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0);
        reg_write : out std_logic;
        mem_write : out std_logic;
        alu_src_a_pc : out std_logic;
        alu_src_b_imm : out std_logic;
        alu_control : out std_logic_vector(3 downto 0);
        branch_enable : out std_logic;
        jump : out std_logic;
        jalr : out std_logic;
        wb_select : out std_logic_vector(1 downto 0)
    );
end entity decoder;
```

## Responsibility
Decode RV32I instruction opcode and function fields into register-write, memory-write, operand-source, ALU-operation, branch, jump, and writeback-selection controls.

## Timing

`decoder` is purely combinational. After `instr` changes, every output shall settle to the value specified below without requiring a clock edge. The decoder has no state, handshake, or latency.

## Reset

None. The decoder has no reset input. Its outputs are determined solely by `instr`.

## Behavior

`instr` is a 32-bit instruction. The decoder uses `instr[6:0]` as the opcode, `instr[14:12]` as `funct3`, and, where specified, `instr[31:25]` as `funct7`.

For every recognized instruction encoding, outputs shall match the instruction-class definitions below. For any unsupported opcode or unsupported function encoding, the instruction shall have no architectural side effects: `reg_write`, `mem_write`, `branch_enable`, `jump`, and `jalr` shall be `'0'`; `alu_src_a_pc` and `alu_src_b_imm` shall be `'0'`; `alu_control` shall be `"0000"`; and `wb_select` shall be `"00"`.

For valid instructions, `reg_write` indicates that the instruction produces a register result. It is asserted for register-writing instruction classes even when `rd` is `x0`; suppression of writes to `x0` is the responsibility of the register-file component. `mem_write` is asserted only for valid stores. `branch_enable` is asserted only for valid conditional branches. `jump` is asserted for `JAL` and `JALR`; `jalr` is asserted only for `JALR`.

`alu_src_a_pc` selects the PC as ALU operand A when `'1'`, and `rs1` otherwise. `alu_src_b_imm` selects the instruction’s applicable immediate as ALU operand B when `'1'`, and `rs2` otherwise. For instructions whose ALU operands do not affect their architectural result, the source controls and ALU control are nevertheless specified below.

Valid instruction classes and their controls:

| Instruction class | `reg_write` | `mem_write` | `alu_src_a_pc` | `alu_src_b_imm` | `branch_enable` | `jump` | `jalr` | `wb_select` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| OP (`0x33`), including RV32M | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| OP-IMM (`0x13`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| Loads (`0x03`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"01"` |
| Stores (`0x23`) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| Conditional branches (`0x63`) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| LUI (`0x37`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| AUIPC (`0x17`) | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `"00"` |
| JAL (`0x6F`) | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | `"10"` |
| JALR (`0x67`, `funct3="000"`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | `"10"` |

The ALU control and operand meaning for each valid class are specified in `Operations`. For JAL and JALR, the ALU control is `"0000"`; jump-target generation is not selected by `alu_control`.

## Operations

`alu_control` is a four-bit selector. Its meaning for non-branch instructions is:

| `alu_control` | Operation |
|---|---|
| `"0000"` | ADD |
| `"0001"` | SUB |
| `"0010"` | SLL |
| `"0011"` | SLT (signed) |
| `"0100"` | SLTU (unsigned) |
| `"0101"` | XOR |
| `"0110"` | SRL |
| `"0111"` | SRA |
| `"1000"` | OR |
| `"1001"` | AND |
| `"1010"` | PASS_B: the result is operand B |
| `"1011"`–`"1111"` | Not selected for non-branch instructions |

When `branch_enable='1'`, `alu_control` instead selects the branch condition:

| `alu_control` | Branch condition |
|---|---|
| `"0000"` | BEQ |
| `"0001"` | BNE |
| `"0010"` | BLT (signed) |
| `"0011"` | BGE (signed) |
| `"0100"` | BLTU (unsigned) |
| `"0101"` | BGEU (unsigned) |

The branch-specific meanings apply only when `branch_enable='1'`.

`wb_select` is a two-bit selector:

| `wb_select` | Writeback source |
|---|---|
| `"00"` | ALU result |
| `"01"` | Data-memory read result |
| `"10"` | `PC + 4` |
| `"11"` | Reserved; never selected by a valid instruction |

| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="110"` | `"1000"` OR | |
| `0x13` OP-IMM | `funct3="111"` | `"1001"` AND | |
| `0x03` Load | `funct3` in `"000"`, `"001"`, `"010"`, `"100"`, `"101"` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x23` Store | `funct3` in `"000"`, `"001"`, `"010"` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="000"` | `"0000"` BEQ | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="001"` | `"0001"` BNE | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="100"` | `"0010"` BLT | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="101"` | `"0011"` BGE | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="110"` | `"0100"` BLTU | |
| `0x63` Branch | `funct3="111"` | `"0101"` BGEU | |
| `0x37` LUI | Any `funct3` and `funct7` | `"1010"` PASS_B | |
| `0x17` AUIPC | Any `funct3` and `funct7` | `"0000"` ADD | |
| `0x6F` JAL | Any `funct3` and `funct7` | `"0000"` | |
| `0x67` JALR | `funct3="000"` | `"0000"` ADD | |

These instructions use the same register-write and operand-source controls as OP, with `wb_select="00"`. For OP and OP-IMM, all function encodings not listed above are unsupported. For loads, stores, branches, and JALR, function encodings not listed above are unsupported. LUI, AUIPC, and JAL do not have function-field restrictions in this contract.

- Any unsupported function combination, including an otherwise recognized opcode with an invalid `funct3` or required `funct7`, produces the no-side-effect outputs defined in `Behavior`.

--- contrato anterior

-- RV32I single cycle

 ISA base: RV32I (lui auipc jal jalr beq bne blt bge bltu bgeu lb lh lw lbu lhu sb sh sw addi slti sltiu xori ori andi slli srli srai add sub sll slt sltu xor srl sra or and).

+RV32M (mul mulh mulhsu mulhu div divu rem remu) is required: decode opcode 0110011 with funct7 = 0000001. Implement these operations in generated VHDL, including RISC-V division-by-zero and signed-overflow semantics. The entity `cpu` has no generics: the ISA is fixed by specs/cpu.md, so the CPU always implements the M instructions.
 Microarchitecture declared in specs/cpu.md: monociclo.
@@ -290,2 +290,79 @@
 
+# RV32M Implementation Reference
+# RV32M — referência de implementação
+
+Fonte: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA, extensão "M" para multiplicação e divisão
+inteiras, versão 2.0 (RISC-V International, CC-BY-4.0).
+
+Este arquivo só vale quando `specs/cpu.md` declara **RV32IM**. Ele completa
+`riscv-rv32i.md`, que continua valendo inteiro: RV32IM = RV32I + M. Com
+**RV32I** este arquivo não vai para a IA e a CPU não implementa nenhuma
+instrução abaixo.
+
+## Codificação
+
+Todas as instruções M são R-type, com `opcode = 0110011` (`0x33`, o mesmo do
+OP do RV32I) e `funct7 = 0000001` (`0x01`). O `funct7` é o que separa M de
+ADD/SUB/shifts/lógica: no RV32I ele vale `0x00` ou `0x20`.
+
+| Instrução | `funct3` | `funct7` | Resultado em `rd` |
+|---|---:|---:|---|
+| MUL | `0x0` | `0x01` | 32 bits baixos de `rs1 × rs2` |
+| MULH | `0x1` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `signed(rs1) × signed(rs2)` |
+| MULHSU | `0x2` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `signed(rs1) × unsigned(rs2)` |
+| MULHU | `0x3` | `0x01` | 32 bits altos de `unsigned(rs1) × unsigned(rs2)` |
+| DIV | `0x4` | `0x01` | quociente signed, arredondado para zero |
+| DIVU | `0x5` | `0x01` | quociente unsigned |
+| REM | `0x6` | `0x01` | resto signed; o sinal é o do dividendo (`rs1`) |
+| REMU | `0x7` | `0x01` | resto unsigned |
+
+## Regras gerais
+
+- O produto completo tem 64 bits. MUL devolve os bits `[31:0]` e é o mesmo
+  para operandos signed ou unsigned. MULH, MULHSU e MULHU devolvem os bits
+  `[63:32]`.
+- MULHSU trata `rs1` como signed e `rs2` como unsigned. Não troque a ordem.
+- Divisão e resto truncam para zero: `-7 / 2 = -3` e `-7 rem 2 = -1`.
+- Nenhuma instrução M gera exceção, trap ou estado extra. `rd = x0` continua
+  sendo ignorado.
+- No contrato monociclo de `specs/cpu.md`, uma instrução completa por borda de
+  subida: o resultado de MUL e DIV precisa estar pronto no mesmo ciclo.
+
+## Casos especiais obrigatórios
+
+A divisão por zero e o overflow têm resultado definido pela ISA. A CPU deve
+produzir exatamente estes valores (`x` é o dividendo `rs1`):
+
+| Caso | DIV | DIVU | REM | REMU |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| divisor = 0 | `-1` (`0xFFFFFFFF`) | `2^32 - 1` (`0xFFFFFFFF`) | `x` | `x` |
+| overflow: `x = -2^31` (`0x80000000`) e divisor = `-1` | `-2^31` (`0x80000000`) | (não se aplica) | `0` | (não se aplica) |
+
+## Exemplos para conferir
+
+| Instrução | `rs1` | `rs2` | `rd` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| MUL | `0x00000007` | `0xFFFFFFFD` (-3) | `0xFFFFFFEB` (-21) |
+| MULH | `0x80000000` | `0x80000000` | `0x40000000` |
+| MULHSU | `0xFFFFFFFF` (-1) | `0xFFFFFFFF` | `0xFFFFFFFF` |
